pages.text: $(bold)Aberrant traits are "double-edged swords": strong positives with a mandatory price.$(0)$(br2)$(bold)【Tier 2 · Aberrations】$(0)$(li)Berserker Gene (berserk_gene): +2 attack, −1.5 armor$(li)Glass Bones (glass_bone): +0.8 attack speed, −2 max health$(br2)$(bold)【Tier 3 · Aberrations】$(0)$(li)Predator Instinct (predator_instinct): +3 attack, +0.02 move speed, −4 max health$(li)Pyroblast Flesh (pyroblast_flesh): +3 attack, $(c)fears fire$(0) — fire damage against you is greatly amplified$(br2)The higher the tier, the more extreme it gets: $(4)the bigger the payoff, the deadlier the price$(0).

$(bold)Once attached, a trait cannot be removed$(0) — aberrations are no exception.$(br2)$(bold)Your two ways out:$(0)$(li)Hand the organ to the "$(l:akaishi:trait_reforger)Trait Reforger$(/l)" to swap that trait in place: it re-rolls within the same tier pool, so the aberration may vanish — or return$(li)Cut your losses and grow a fresh organ on the organ line$(br2)$(bold)Reminder:$(0) aberrations are not a bug — they are a high-risk, high-reward play. Building around them usually beats endlessly re-rolling. If you gamble, be ready to win or lose.
Suggested order: aberrations roll from the same pool as safe traits — compare catalogs in "Safe Mutations"; use the "Trait Reforger" to swap an aberration away (or into) an organ.
